These factors always occur in pairs (ALGEBRA, § 179.) and have this form $$x+a+\beta\sqrt{-1}, \quad x-a-\beta\sqrt{-1},$$ so that their product $$x^2 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2$$ is a real factor of the second degree. As every corresponding <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-PAIR">pair</a> of imaginary simple factors may be united in this manner into a real factor of the second degree, if these factors are all unequal, we may avoid introducing imaginary quantities into the fluent of the proposed fraction by proceeding thus. Let $x+a+\beta\sqrt{-1}$ and $x+a-\beta\sqrt{-1}$ denote two corresponding imaginary simple factors of the denominator. Instead of the two simple fractions $$\frac{N}{x+a+\beta\sqrt{-1}}, \quad \frac{N'}{x+a-\beta\sqrt{-1}},$$ which would have been assumed if the factors had been real, assume a single fraction $$\frac{(Kx+L)}{x^2 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2}$$ the denominator of which is a real function of $x$ of the second degree, viz. that which is the product of the two imaginary factors. Here $K$ and $L$ denote two constant but indeterminate coefficients, the values of which, as also those of the other indeterminate coefficients are to be found as before. If the denominator of the proposed fraction have several equal factors of the second degree resulting from its imaginary simple factors, so that the product of those equal factors is $$(x^2 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2)^p,$$ then, corresponding to this product, we must, among the fractions having indeterminate coefficients, assume one of this form $$\frac{(Qx^2 + R'x + \cdots + Y')}{(x^2 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2)^p},$$ where $Q', R', \ldots Y'$ denote constant and indeterminate coefficients, the values of which will be found in all respects as those of the others. We are now to find the fluents of these two fluxional expressions, beginning with the first, viz. $$\frac{(Kx+L)}{x^2 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2} \text{ or } \frac{(Kx+L)}{(x+a)^2 + \beta^2}.$$ Put $x+a=z$, then it becomes $$\frac{(Kz+L-Kz)}{z^2 + \beta^2};$$ and this again, by putting $L-Kz=M$, is resolved into these two fluions $$\frac{Kz}{z^2 + \beta^2} + \frac{M}{z^2 + \beta^2}.$$ We can immediately find the fluent of the first of these, by putting $z^2 + \beta^2=v$, for then $z=\frac{v}{2}$, and $$\int \frac{Kz}{z^2 + \beta^2} = \frac{K}{2} \int \frac{v}{v} = K \cdot \frac{1}{v} \cdot v, (\S 103),$$ $$= K \cdot \frac{1}{v} \cdot (z^2 + \beta^2).$$ With respect to the other fluxion, if we put $z=\beta y$, we have $$\frac{M}{z^2 + \beta^2} = \frac{M}{\beta^2 + y^2},$$ but we have seen ($\S 60$) that $\frac{y}{1+y^2}$ is the fluxion of an arch of which the tangent is $y$, therefore $$\int \frac{M}{\beta^2 + y^2} = \frac{M}{\beta} \arctan(y) + \text{const.}$$ $$= \frac{M}{\beta} \arctan\left(\frac{x}{\beta}\right) + \text{const.}$$ It is proper to remark, that if $\frac{x}{\beta}$ be the tangent of an arch, then the sine of that arch is $\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + \beta^2}}$, and its cosine is $\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{x^2 + \beta^2}}$, thus we may express the fluent under different forms, by introducing the sine or cosine of the arch instead of its tangent. If instead of \( x \) we substitute in these two fluents \( x + a \) we find that the fluent of \( \frac{(Kx+L)x}{x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2} \) is \[ K \cdot \sqrt{x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2} \\ + \frac{L-Ka}{\beta} \text{ arc } (\tan = \frac{x+a}{\beta}) + \text{const.} \] 114. To find the fluent of the expression \[ \frac{(Q'x^{q-1}+R'x^{q-2}+\ldots+Y')x}{(x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2)^q}, \] we first transform it to \[ \frac{(Kx+L)x}{(x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2)} \\ + \frac{(K'x+L')x}{(x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} \\ \ldots + \frac{(K''x+\ldots+L''\ldots)x}{x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2}, \] where \( K, L, K', L', \ldots \) denote indeterminate but constant coefficients, which may be determined by reducing these fractions to a common denominator, and proceeding as in the two preceding §§. Then the whole difficulty is reduced to the finding of the fluxion of the expression \[ \frac{(Kx+L)x}{(x^2+2ax+a^2+\beta^2)^q} = \frac{(Kx+L)x}{((x+a)^2+\beta^2)^q}, \] where \( q \) denotes some integer number. To simplify this expression put \( x+a=z \), and \( L-Ka=M \), then it becomes \[ \frac{(Kz+M)z}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q}, \] which we shall now shew may be reduced to \( \int \frac{Hx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} \). To effect this <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-REDUCTION">reduction</a> we decompose its fluent into two parts \[ \int \frac{Kxz}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} + \int \frac{Mx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q}. \] The fluent of the first part may be immediately found by putting \( z^2+\beta^2=v \); for then \( xz=\frac{v}{2} \) and \[ \int \frac{Kxz}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} = \int \frac{Kv}{2v^q} = \frac{Ke^{-\frac{v}{2}}}{2(1-q)}. \] Let us now suppose that the fluent of the second part \( \frac{Mx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} \) is equal to the sum of the algebraic function \[ G(x^2+\beta^2)^{-q}, \quad \text{and another function, which is the fluent} \] of \( \frac{Hx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} \), that is, let us assume \[ \int \frac{Mx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} = \frac{Gx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} + \int \frac{Hx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}}, \] where \( G \) and \( H \) are constant but indeterminate coefficients. To determine these, let the fluxion of each side of this equation be taken (observing that the fluxion of a quantity having the sign \( \int \) prefixed to it is the same quantity only without that sign); thus we have \[ \frac{Mx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} = \frac{Gx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} - \frac{2(q-1)Gx^2}{(z^2+\beta^2)} \\ + \frac{Hx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}}, \] and from this equation, by rejecting what is common to each term, we find \[ M = G(z^2+\beta^2) - 2(q-1)Gx^2 + H(z^2+\beta^2), \] and hence \[ M = G\beta^2 + H\beta^2 + (G-2(q-1)G+H)x^2; \] Therefore by comparing together like terms, we find \[ M = G\beta^2 + H\beta^2, \quad G-2(q-1)G+H=0; \] and from these equations we get \[ G = \frac{M}{(2q-2)\beta^2}, \quad H = \frac{(2q-3)M}{(2q-2)\beta^2}. \] Let these values of \( G \) and \( H \) be now substituted in our assumed equation, and it becomes \[ \int \frac{Mx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} = \frac{M}{(2q-2)\beta^2} \frac{z}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} \\ + \frac{M(2q-3)}{(2q-2)\beta^2} \int \frac{z}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}}. \] Thus we have reduced the determination of the fluent of \( \frac{Mx}{(z^2+\beta^2)^q} \) to that of \( \frac{z}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-1}} \), and by proceeding in the same manner with this last fluxion, its fluent may be made to depend on that of \( \frac{z}{(z^2+\beta^2)^{q-2}} \); but this will be more readily effected by simply substituting \( q-1 \) instead of \( q \), and supposing \( M=1 \) in the preceding equation. Thus Thus we shall obtain \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-1}} = \frac{1}{(2q-4)\beta^4} \left( x^2 + \beta^2 \right)^{-q+2} \] \[ + \frac{(2q-5)}{(2q-4)\beta^4} \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-2}}. \] Substituting now this value of \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-1}} \) in the former equation, we have \( \int \frac{M\dot{x}}{(x^2 + B^2)^q} \) equal to \[ \frac{M}{(2q-2)\beta^2} \left( x^2 + \beta^2 \right)^{-q+1} \] \[ = \frac{(2q-3)M}{(2q-2)(2q-4)\beta^4} \left( x^2 + \beta^2 \right)^{-q+2} \] \[ + \frac{(2q-3)(2q-5)M}{(2q-2)(2q-4)\beta^4} \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-2}}. \] It is easy to see, that like as we obtained an expression for the fluent of \( \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-1}} \) by substituting \( q-1 \) for \( q \), and supposing \( M=1 \), in the equation preceding the last but one; so by substituting \( q-2 \) for \( q \), we shall obtain an expression for the fluent of \( \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-2}} \), which expression will consist of two terms, one an algebraic function of \( x \), and the other \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-3}} \) multiplied by a constant and given coefficient. This value of \( \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-2}} \) when substituted in the last equation will produce an expression for \( \int \frac{M\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^q} \) consisting of algebraic quantities and \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^{q-3}} \). By continuing this <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-PROCESS">process</a> it is evident that we shall at last have \( \int \frac{M\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)^q} \) expressed by a series of algebraic quantities, and \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{x^2 + \beta^2} \), and here we must stop, for if we repeat the process with a view to make the fluent depend on \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{(x^2 + \beta^2)} \) that is on \( \int \dot{x} \), or \( x \), we shall find that the coefficient of this quantity becomes infinite. As to the fluent of \( \frac{\dot{x}}{x^2 + \beta^2} \) we have exhibited the expression for it in last §. In comparing together the results which have been obtained in the preceding <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-ARTICLES">articles</a>, it must appear that when a fluxion is expressed by a rational fraction, if we <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-GRANT">grant</a> the resolution of equations, the fluent may always be assigned either algebraically, or by means of <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-ARCHES">arches</a> of a circle or logarithms; and that to prepare it for a solution, we must decompose the fraction into others, whose denominators may be either binomial or trinomial quantities. This decomposition may always be effected by the method of indeterminate coefficients. There are, however, several analytical artifices by which the labour of calculation may be greatly shortened. These we now proceed to explain. 115. Let us recur to the fraction \( \frac{U}{V} \), and suppose that \( x+a \) is one of the unequal factors of the denominator \( V \), so that we have \( V=(x+a)Q \). Let us now put \( \frac{U}{V} = \frac{A}{x+a} + \frac{P}{Q} \), \( A \) being supposed a constant quantity, and \( P \) an indeterminate function of \( x \), but such as not to be divisible by \( x+a \). Then we have \( U=AQ+P(x+a) \), and hence \( P=\frac{U-AQ}{x+a} \). As \( P \) is an integer function with respect to \( x \), it follows from this equation that \( U-AQ \), which is also a rational and integer function of \( x \), is divisible by \( x+a \), and consequently has \( x+a \) for a factor; therefore, the function \( U-AQ \) will vanish when we substitute \(-a\) in it instead of \( x \), seeing that \(-a\) is the value of \( x \) that makes the factor \( x+a=0 \). Let us denote by \( u \) and \( q \), what \( U \) and \( Q \) become by this substitution, which however will not affect the indeterminate quantity \( A \), because it is independent of \( x \). We have therefore \( u-Aq=0 \), and consequently \( A=\frac{u}{q} \). This value of \( A \) requires that we should know the function \( Q \) given by the equation \( V=(x+a)Q \), and we may always find it by dividing \( V \) by \( x+a \). The direct method of fluxions affords also a very simple method of determining it. For by taking the fluxion of the above equation we have \[ \frac{\dot{V}}{x} = Q+(x+a)\frac{\dot{Q}}{x}; \] if in this result we make \( x+a=0 \), or \( x=-a \), and denote by \( v \) what \( \frac{\dot{V}}{x} \) becomes by that substitution, we shall have \( v=q \), and consequently \( A=\frac{u}{v} \). The expression \( A=\frac{u}{q} \) has always a finite value, for the numerator and denominator can never become \( =0 \), because we suppose the fraction \( \frac{U}{V} \) reduced to its lowest terms, and consequently, that the numerator \( U \) has not for a factor \( x+a \), which is a factor of the denominator, but which being contained in it only once does not enter into \( Q \). 116. Let us now consider how the numerators of the fractions, into which the proposed fraction \( \frac{U}{V} \) is to be decomposed, are to be found in the case of the denomi- The direct method of fluxions facilitates greatly the preceding operations. For the numerator of \( P \) being divisible by \((x+a)^n\) is necessarily of this form \( X(x+a)^n \), \( X \) being an integer function of \( x \), but which does not contain the factor \( x+a \). Now agreeably to what has been shown in § 88, the successive fluxions of this numerator, as far as the \( n-1 \) order inclusive, vanish when \( x-a \) is supposed \( = 0 \). By giving to the numerator the following form, \[ Q \left( \frac{U}{Q} - A - B(x+a) - C(x+a)^2 - \ldots \right) \] and observing that the function \( Q \) does not contain the factor \( x+a \), it is manifest that it is only the part of this expression between the parentheses which ought to be divisible by \((x+a)^n\). Let us put \( \frac{U}{Q} = Z \), then the successive fluxions of that part are \[ Z - Bx^2 - 2C(x+a)x^3 - 3D(x+a)^2x^4 - \ldots \] and these results ought all to vanish when we put \( x+a=0 \). Thus we have \[ Z-A=0, \quad A=\frac{u}{q}, \quad \frac{Z}{x}=B, \quad \frac{Z}{x^2}=C, \quad \frac{Z}{x^3}=D, \quad \text{&c.} \] Observing that in each of these functions \( \frac{Z}{x}, \frac{Z}{x^2}, \frac{Z}{x^3} \), we must substitute \( -a \) instead of \( x \). The most simple way to find the value of \( Q \) in this case is to divide \( V \) by \((x+a)^n\); but we may also find it by the direct method of fluxions, as in the preceding §; for, since \( V=Q(x+a)^n \), if we take the fluxion of each side of this equation \( n \) times, and then make \( x+a=0 \), we shall find, § 88, the \( n \)th fluxion of \( V \) equal to \( 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot \ldots \cdot n \cdot Q \cdot x^n \), and consequently \[ Q = \frac{n \text{th <a class="xref" href="vol8.html#article-FLUX">flux</a>. of } V}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdot \ldots \cdot n \cdot x^n} \] 117. Let us now consider how we are to find the numerator of the fraction which forms a part of \( \frac{U}{V} \) when it has this form \[ \frac{A(x+a)}{x^2 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta} \] Assume Assume \[ U = \frac{Ax + B}{x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3} + P; \] then, reducing the latter part of this equation to a common denominator, we find \[ U = Q(Ax + B) + P(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3). \] Hence we deduce \[ P = \frac{U - Q(Ax + B)}{x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3}. \] As \( P \) is supposed to be an integer function with respect to \( x \), it follows that \( U - Q(Ax + B) \) is divisible by \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 \); therefore, the former of these two quantities must contain among its factors those of the latter, and the quantities, which, being substituted for \( x \), cause the latter to vanish, must also make the former vanish. But the factors of \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 \) are \( x + a + b\sqrt{-1} \) and \( x + a - b\sqrt{-1} \), and these, being put each \( = 0 \), gives us \( x = -(a + b\sqrt{-1}) \) and \( x = -(a - b\sqrt{-1}) \); therefore, each of these values of \( x \) being substituted in \( U - Q(Ax + B) \) ought to make that quantity vanish. Let us denote by \( u = a + b\sqrt{-1} \) and by \( q = a - b\sqrt{-1} \) what \( U \) and \( Q \) respectively become when \( -(a + b\sqrt{-1}) \) is substituted in each instead of \( x \); then, after this transformation, we have \[ -(q - q'\sqrt{-1}) \left\{ -A(a + b\sqrt{-1}) + B \right\} = 0. \] This equation is twofold, because of the sign \( = \) with which several of its terms are affected, and it is <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol2.html#article-EQUIVALENT">equivalent</a> to those which would be formed by putting the real part equal to 0, and the imaginary part \( = 0 \); from this consideration we have \[ u + q = A - q'A - qB = 0, \] \[ u' + q' = A + q'A + q'B = 0, \] two equations which give us the values of \( A \) and \( B \). The function \( Q \) may be found as in § 115. For, if we take the fluxions of each side of the equation \[ Q(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3) = V, \] and afterwards make \[ x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 = 0, \] we find \( Q(2x + 2a) = V \), and hence \[ Q = \frac{V}{2x + 2a}. \] Let the two values of \( x \), to <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-WIT">wit</a> \( -(a + b\sqrt{-1}) \), be substituted instead of it in this equation, then, putting \( u = a + b\sqrt{-1} \) to denote what the expression \( \frac{V}{x} \) becomes by that substitution, and writing \( q = a - b\sqrt{-1} \) instead of \( Q \), we have \[ q = q'\sqrt{-1} = e^{i\sqrt{-1}}, \] \[ = 2b\sqrt{-1}, \] which, by multiplying the terms of the fraction on the latter side of the equation by \( \sqrt{-1} \), becomes \[ q = q'\sqrt{-1} = \frac{e^{i\sqrt{-1}}}{2b}. \] Hence by putting the real parts of each side of this equation equal to each other, and also the imaginary parts equal to each other, we find \[ q = \frac{v'}{2b}, \quad q' = \frac{v}{2b}. \] 118. If the factor \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 \) is found several times in the denominator of \( V \), so that \[ V = Q(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3)^n, \] then, § 113, we assume in this case \( \frac{U}{V} \) equal to \[ \frac{Ax + B}{(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3)^n} + \frac{A'x + B'}{(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3)^{n-1}} + \cdots + \frac{P}{Q}. \] Reducing this expression to a common denominator, and so ordering the equation as to bring \( P \) to stand alone on one side, we find \( P \) equal to \[ U = Q \left\{ Ax + B + (A'x + B')(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3) + \cdots \right\} \] \[ (x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3)^n. \] By reasoning in this as in the preceding case, it may be concluded that the numerator of this expression ought to vanish when \( -(a + b\sqrt{-1}) \) is substituted in it instead of \( x \); therefore putting \( u = a + b\sqrt{-1} \), and \( q = a - b\sqrt{-1} \) to denote the same things as before, we deduce from that substitution \[ -(q - q'\sqrt{-1}) \left\{ -A(a + b\sqrt{-1}) + B \right\} = 0. \] The very same equation for the determination of \( A \) and \( B \), as we have already found in last §. Having found the values of these quantities, they may be substituted in the numerator of \( P \), and the terms \( U = Q(Ax + B) \) becoming divisible by \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 \), the whole expression becomes divisible by the same quantity. Calling therefore \( U' \) the quotient arising from the <a class="xref" href="vol7.html#article-DIVISION">division</a> of \( U = Q(Ax + B) \) by \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 \), we have \( P \) equal to \[ U' = Q[Ax + B + (A'x + B')(x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3) + \cdots] \] \[ (x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3)^n. \] If in this numerator we substitute instead of \( x \) its values deduced from the equation \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 = 0 \), and put the result \( = 0 \), we may determine \( A' \) and \( B' \) in the very same way that we have already determined \( A \) and \( B \), and by proceeding in this manner we shall find the remaining coefficients \( A'' \), \( B'' \), &c. This case is quite analogous to that which has been already treated in § 116, and the direct method of fluxions applies to it in the same manner as to the other. For since \( Q \) does not contain the factor \( x^3 + 2ax + a^3 + b^3 \), if the numerator of \( P \) be divided by the function \( Q \), the result, which may be denoted by \( r \), ought to be of this form. Inverse form \( r = X(x^3 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2) \), and consequently ought to vanish, as well as all its fluxions, from the first order to the \( n-1 \) order, inclusively, when \( x^3 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2 = 0 \); this being the case, we have these equations, \[ r = 0, \quad r' = 0, \quad r'' = 0, \ldots \] and so on to the \( n-1 \) fluxion of \( r \), which ought also to be \( = 0 \); each of these equations becomes twofold when we substitute, instead of \( x \), the values of which it is susceptible in <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-CONSEQUENCE">consequence</a> of the equation \( x^3 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2 = 0 \). By putting the real and the imaginary parts separately \( = 0 \), we shall obtain as many equations as are sufficient to determine \( A, B, A', B' \), &c. It may also be remarked, that from the equation \[ V = Q(x^3 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2)^n \] we find \( Q \) equal to the quotient arising from the division of the \( n \)th fluxion of \( V \) by the \( n \)th fluxion of \( x^3 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2 \), observing to assume \[ x^3 + 2ax + a^2 + \beta^2 = 0. \] 119. We shall now give some applications of what has been said relative to the fluents of rational fractions. Suppose the fraction to be \[ \frac{x}{x^3 + x^2 - x^4 - x^5}. \] The factors of its denominator are easily found, for it may be put under this form \[ x(x^3 + x^2 - x - 1) = x(x+1)(x^2 - 1), \] the factor \( x^2 - 1 \) may be decomposed into \( x - 1 \) and \( x + 1 \), or \( x - 1, x + 1 \), and \( x^2 + 1 \), thus we have the denominator equal to \[ x(x-1)(x+1)(x^2 + 1) \] therefore (§ 111, § 112, and § 113,) the proposed fraction is to be decomposed as follows \[ \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{(x+1)^2} + \frac{C}{x+1} + \frac{D}{x^3} + \frac{E}{x^2} + \frac{F}{x} + \frac{(Gx+H)x}{1+x^3} \] By reducing these fractions to a common denominator, and comparing the numerator of their sum with that of the proposed fraction, we might determine the unknown quantities \( A, B, C, \) &c., we shall, however, rather employ the methods that have <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-JUST">just</a> been explained. By comparing this particular example \( \frac{x}{x^3 + x^2 - x^4 - x^5} \) with the general expression \( \frac{U}{V} \), it appears that \( U = 1 \), and \( V = x^3 + x^2 - x^4 - x^5 \). First let us investigate the numerator of the fraction \( \frac{A}{x-1} \), and for this purpose we employ the formula \( A = \frac{u}{v} \) (§ 115.). As we have \( U = 1 \), it is evident that \( u = 1 \); and since \( V = x^3 + x^2 \) \[ -x^4 - x^5, \text{ therefore } \frac{V}{x} = 8x^7 + 7x^6 - 4x^5 - 3x^4. \] If in this expression we substitute \( -1 \) instead of \( x \) (viz. the value of \( x \) deduced from the equation \( x - 1 = 0 \)) we find the result to be 8, therefore \( v = 8 \). So that \[ A = \frac{u}{v} = \frac{1}{8} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{A}{x-1} = \frac{1}{8} \frac{1}{x-1}. \] Let us next investigate the values of \( B \) and \( C \) in the fractions \( \frac{B}{(x+1)^2} \) and \( \frac{C}{x+1} \), by means of the rule of § 116, and that we may make the symbols expressing the quantity under consideration agree with those employed in that formula, let us <a class="xref" href="vol8.html#article-EXCHANGE">exchange</a> the letters \( B \) and \( C \) for \( A \) and \( B_1 \) so that we are to consider \( \frac{A}{(x+1)^2} + \frac{B}{x+1} \). In the first place we have \[ Q = \frac{x^3 + x^2 - x^4 - x^5}{(x+1)^2} = x^3 + x^2 - x^4 - x^5; \] Put \( x + 1 = 0 \), then \( x = 1 \); substituting now this value of \( x \) in the value of \( Q \), the result is 4, therefore \[ A = \frac{u}{v} = \frac{1}{4}. \] Let this value of \( A \) be substituted for \( A \) in the expression for \( U' \) in the § above cited, and we have \[ U' = \frac{U-AQ}{x+1} = \frac{4-x^3+x^2-x^4+x^5}{4(x+1)} = \frac{-x^3+2x^4-3x^5+4x^6-4x+4}{4}. \] Hence putting \( -1 \) instead of \( x \) in the expression for \( U' \), we have \( u' = \frac{9}{2} \) and \( B = \frac{u'}{q} = \frac{9}{8} \). Thus the two fractions under consideration are found to be \( \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{(x+1)^2} \) and \( \frac{9}{8} \cdot \frac{1}{x+1} \). We might have deduced the value of \( B \) from the formula \( B = \frac{Z}{x} \), § 116, where \( Z \) is put for \( \frac{U}{Q} \), for we have \[ Z = \frac{U}{Q} = \frac{1}{(x^3 - x^2 + x^4 - x^5)}, \] and \( \frac{Z}{x} = \frac{6x^5 - 5x^4 + 4x^3 - 3x^2}{(x^6 - x^5 + x^4 - x^3)^2} \). If in this expression we substitute \( -1 \) instead of \( x \), it becomes \( \frac{18}{16} = \frac{9}{8} \), the same value for \( B \) as before. Let us now consider the fractions \( \frac{D}{x^3} + \frac{E}{x^2} + \frac{F}{x} \), or exchanging the symbols \( D, E, F \) for \( A, B, C \), \[ \frac{A}{x^3} + \frac{B}{x^2} + \frac{C}{x}. \] The numerators \( A, B, C \) may all be found from these formulas of § 116. A = \frac{U}{Q} = Z, B = \frac{Z}{x}, C = \frac{Z}{1.2x^2}, observing that in this case Q = x^5 + x^4 - x - 1; and that we must substitute o instead of x in each formula, after taking the fluxions. Now we have \[ Z = \frac{U}{Q} = \frac{x}{x^5 + x^4 - x - 1}, \] \[ \dot{Z} = \frac{5x^4 + 4x^3 - 1}{(x^5 + x^4 - x - 1)^2}, \] \[ \ddot{Z} = \frac{20x^3 + 12x^2}{(x^5 + x^4 - x - 1)^3} + \frac{2(5x^4 + 4x^3 - 1)}{(x^5 + x^4 - x - 1)^3}; \] Hence putting \( x = 0 \), we find \[ A = -1, B = +1, C = -1, \] so that \[ \frac{A}{x^3} + \frac{B}{x^2} + \frac{C}{x} = -\frac{1}{x^3} + \frac{1}{x^2} - \frac{1}{x}. \] There yet remains the fraction \( \frac{Gx + H}{x^2 + 1} \), or \( \frac{Ax + B}{x^2 + 1} \) to be considered. It may be found by subtracting the sum of all the others from the proposed fraction; we proceed, however, to find it directly by the formulas of § 117. In the first place we have \( Q = x^6 + x^5 - x^4 - x^3 \); next, the factor \( x^2 + 1 \) being put \( = 0 \) gives \( x = \pm \sqrt{-1} \). Hence we find \[ q = \sqrt{-1} = -2\sqrt{-1}, u = 1, \text{ and } w = 0. \] The equations which determine A and B thus become \[ 1 + 2A + 2B = 0, \quad 2A - 2B = 0, \] therefore \( A = B = -\frac{1}{4} \), and \[ \frac{Ax + B}{x^2 + 1} = -\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{x + 1}{x^2 + 1}. \] Thus, upon the whole, the proposed fraction \[ \frac{x}{x^6 + x^5 - x^4 - x^3} \] is decomposed into the following \[ \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x}{x-1} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right)^2 + \frac{9}{8} \frac{x}{x+1} \right) \] \[ = \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x}{x^3 + x^2 - x - 1} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right)^2 + \frac{9}{8} \frac{x}{x+1} \right). \] The manner of finding the fluent of each of these has been already explained, and the result of taking all the fluents is \[ \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x}{x-1} - \frac{1}{4} \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right) + \frac{9}{8} \left( \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right) + \frac{1}{4} \arctan(x) + \text{const}. \] The union of all the algebraic terms produces the inverse fraction \( \frac{2 - 2x - 5x^3}{4x^2(1+x)} \), and that of the logarithmic quantities gives \[ \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x}{x-1} + \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right)^2 + \frac{9}{8} \frac{x}{x+1} \right) \] \[ = \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x}{x^3 + x^2 - x - 1} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right)^2 + \frac{9}{8} \frac{x}{x+1} \right). \] We have therefore upon the whole \( \int \frac{x}{x^6 + x^5 - x^4 - x^3} \) equal to \[ \frac{2 - 2x - 5x^3}{4x^2(1+x)} + \frac{1}{8} \left( \frac{x}{x^3 + x^2 - x - 1} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \frac{x+1}{x^2+1} \right)^2 + \frac{9}{8} \frac{x}{x+1} \right) \] \[ + \frac{1}{4} \arctan(x) + \text{const}. \] 120 When a fluxion is a rational fraction having either of these forms \[ \frac{x^n}{x^n + a^n}, \quad \frac{x^n}{x^n + 2p a^n x^n + a^n}, \] we can always, by the application of a particular theorem in <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-ANALYSIS">analysis</a>, resolve its denominator into real factors of the first and second degrees. The theorem to which we allude is this. Let \( n \) be any positive integer, and let \( z \) denote any arch of a circle, of which the radius is unity, then \[ (\cos(z) + \sqrt{-1} \sin(z))^n = \cos(nz) + \sqrt{-1} \sin(nz). \] We proceed to prove this theorem. Because \[ (\cos(z) + \sqrt{-1} \sin(z))(\cos(z) - \sqrt{-1} \sin(z)) = \cos^2(z) + \sin^2(z) = 1. \] If we put \( \cos(z) + \sqrt{-1} \sin(z) = v, \) Then \( \cos(z) - \sqrt{-1} \sin(z) = \frac{1}{v}; \) Therefore taking the sum of these two equations, \[ 2 \cos(z) = v + \frac{1}{v}. \] Now by the <a class="xref" href="vol2.html#article-ARITHMETIC">arithmetic</a> of sines, (ALGEBRA, § 358.) \[ 2 \cos(2z) = 2(2 \cos(z) \times \cos(z) - 1), \] \[ 2 \cos(3z) = 2(2 \cos(z) \times \cos(z) \times \cos(z) - \cos(z)), \] \[ 2 \cos(4z) = 2(2 \cos(z) \times \cos(z) \times \cos(z) \times \cos(z) - \cos(2z)), \] \[ 2 \cos(5z) = 2(2 \cos(z) \times \cos(z) \times \cos(z) \times \cos(z) \times \cos(z) - \cos(3z)), \] &c. Therefore, substituting in the first of these equations \( v + \frac{1}{v} \) instead of \( 2 \cos(z) \), we have \[ 2 \cos(z). \] In like manner, substituting in the second equation, \( v + \frac{1}{v} \) instead of \( 2 \cos x \), and \( v^2 + \frac{1}{v^2} \) instead of \( 2 \cos 2x \), we have \[ 2 \cos 3x = (v + \frac{1}{v})(v + \frac{1}{v^2}) - (v + \frac{1}{v}) \] \[ = v^3 + \frac{1}{v^3}. \] Proceeding in the same way with the third and following equations, we find \[ 2 \cos 4x = v^4 + \frac{1}{v^4}, \] \[ 2 \cos 5x = v^5 + \frac{1}{v^5}; \] so that we may conclude in general that \[ 2 \cos nx = v^n + \frac{1}{v^n}; \] hence we have this quadratic equation \[ v^n - 2 \cos nx + v^n + 1 = 0, \] from which, by completing the <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-SQUARE">square</a>, we find \[ v^n = \cos nx \pm \sqrt{(\cos^2 nx - 1)}; \] therefore, by substituting for \( v \) the quantity it was put to represent, and observing that \( \sqrt{\cos^2 nx - 1} = \sqrt{-1 \sin nx} \), we have \[ (\cos nx \pm \sqrt{-1 \sin nx})^n = \cos nx \pm \sqrt{-1 \sin nx}, \] as was to be proved. 121. The function \( x^n = a^n \) is transformed to \( a^n (y^n - 1) \) by putting \( x = <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-AY">ay</a> \), and to discover its factors, we must resolve the equation \[ y^n - 1 = 0. \] The expression \( y = \cos x + \sqrt{-1 \sin x} \) satisfies this equation, by a very simple determination of the arch \( x \); for we have \( y^n = (\cos x + \sqrt{-1 \sin x})^n = \cos nx + \sqrt{-1 \sin nx} \), and as by putting \( \pi \) to denote half the circumference, and \( m \) any whole number, we have (ALGEBRA, § 352.) \[ \sin m \pi = 0, \quad \cos m \pi = \pm 1, \] where the sign \( \pm \) is to be taken, if \( m \) be an even number, but \( - \) if it be odd, we have only to suppose \( n \pi = m \pi \), in order to obtain \( y^n = 1 \). That we may distinguish the case in which \( m \) is even, \[ 2 \cos 2x = (v + \frac{1}{v})(v + \frac{1}{v^2}) - 2 \] \[ = v^3 + \frac{1}{v^3}. \] from that in which it is odd, we shall write for the first \( 2m \), and for the second \( 2m + 1 \); we therefore make \[ n \pi = 2m \pi, \quad n \pi = (2m + 1) \pi. \] By the first hypothesis, we find \[ y^n = 1, \quad y = \cos \frac{2m \pi}{n} + \sqrt{-1 \sin \frac{2m \pi}{n}}, \] and by the second \[ y^n = -1, \] \[ y = \cos \frac{(2m + 1) \pi}{n} + \sqrt{-1 \sin \frac{(2m + 1) \pi}{n}}. \] 122. By means of the indeterminate number \( m \), each of these expressions for \( y \) furnishes all the values of which this quantity is susceptible, for we may take successively \[ m = 0, \quad m = 1, \quad m = 2, \quad m = 3, \quad \text{&c.} \] The first formula gives \[ y = \cos 0 \cdot \pi = 1 \] \[ y = \cos \frac{2\pi}{n} + \sqrt{-1 \sin \frac{2\pi}{n}}, \] \[ y = \cos \frac{4\pi}{n} + \sqrt{-1 \sin \frac{4\pi}{n}}, \] &c. It is evident that we shall always have different results as far as \( m = n - 1 \). If, however, we suppose \( m = n \); then we have \( y = \cos 2 \pi = 1 \), which is the same as the first of the values already obtained, and if we suppose \( m = n + 1 \), then (ALGEBRA, § 25.) \[ \cos \frac{(2n + 2)\pi}{n} = \cos \left(2\pi + \frac{2\pi}{n}\right) = \cos \frac{2\pi}{n}, \] \[ \sin \frac{(2n + 2)\pi}{n} = \sin \left(2\pi + \frac{2\pi}{n}\right) = \sin \frac{2\pi}{n}, \] which is the same as the second value, and so on with respect to the others. By this mode of proceeding we shall not only obtain the \( n \) roots of the equation \( y^n = 1 \), or \( y^n - 1 = 0 \), but, with a little <a class="xref" href="vol3.html#article-ATTENTION">attention</a>, we shall discover that these roots may be arranged in pairs, by bringing together those that only differ in the sign of the radical \( \sqrt{-1} \); for since \[ \cos (2\pi - p) = \cos p, \quad \sin (2\pi - p) = -\sin p, \] it follows that \[ y = \cos \frac{(2n - 2m)\pi}{n} + \sqrt{-1 \sin \frac{(2n - 2m)\pi}{n}} \] \[ = \cos \frac{2m \pi}{n} - \sqrt{-1 \sin \frac{2m \pi}{n}}. \] Hence it appears that we may comprehend all the roots of the equation \( y^n = 1 \) in the single expressions The first and the last of the factors of the second degree are the squares of \( y - 1 \) and \( y + 1 \), factors of the first degree, each of which only enters once into the proposed function; it will therefore be necessary, when we employ the factors of the second degree, to reject the first and last, and take instead of them \[ (y - 1)(y + 1) = y^2 - 1. \] The factors of the first degree of the function \( y^2 - 1 \) are \[ y - 1, \] \[ y - (\cos \frac{2\pi}{5} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{2\pi}{5}), \] \[ y - (\cos \frac{4\pi}{5} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{4\pi}{5}). \] Those of the third degree are \[ y^3 - 2y + 1, \] \[ y^3 - 2y \cos \frac{2\pi}{5} + 1, \] \[ y^3 - 2y \cos \frac{4\pi}{5} + 1; \] but it is to be observed that the first factor of the second degree is the square of \( y - 1 \), which enters only once into the proposed function. 123. When the function to be decomposed into factors is \( y^2 + 1 \), the formula \[ y = \cos \frac{(2m+1)\pi}{n} + \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{(2m+1)\pi}{n}, \] which corresponds to that case (§ 121.) is also susceptible of the <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-DOUBLE">double</a> sign \( \pm \), provided we stop at the value of \( m \), which gives \[ 2m + 1 = n, \text{ or } 2m + 1 = n - 1, \] according as \( n \) is odd or even; hence it follows that \[ m = \frac{n-1}{2}, \quad m = \frac{n-2}{2}; \] the factors of the first degree are \[ y - (\cos \frac{(2m+1)\pi}{n} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{(2m+1)\pi}{n}), \] and those of the second \[ y^3 - 2y \cos \frac{(2m+1)\pi}{n} + 1. \] When among these last there is found some which are squares, we must take only one of their simple factors, in the same way as in the two preceding examples. When the function is \( y^2 + 1 \), the factors of the first degree are \[ y - (\cos \frac{\pi}{5} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{\pi}{5}), \] \[ y - (\cos \frac{3\pi}{5} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{3\pi}{5}) \] \( y + 1; \) and and those of the second, \[ y^2 - 2y \cos \frac{\pi}{5} + 1, \] \[ y^2 - 2y \cos \frac{3\pi}{5} + 1, \] \[ y^2 + 2y + 1. \] The function \( y^2 + 1 \) has for factors of the first degree \[ y = (\cos \frac{\pi}{6} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{\pi}{6}), \] \[ y = (\cos \frac{3\pi}{6} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{3\pi}{6}), \] \[ y = (\cos \frac{5\pi}{6} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{5\pi}{6}). \] and those of the second, \[ y^2 - 2y \cos \frac{\pi}{6} + 1, \] \[ y^2 - 2y \cos \frac{3\pi}{6} + 1, \text{ or } y^2 + 1, \] \[ y^2 - 2y \cos \frac{5\pi}{6} + 1. \] 124. Such functions as are of this form \( x^n + 2px^n + q \) may be treated in the same manner as those which consist of only two terms. By putting the function \( = 0 \), and resolving the equation which is thus produced, in the same manner as if it were of the second degree, we find the factors to be \[ x^n + (p \pm \sqrt{(p^2 - q)}); \] if \( p^2 > q \), the second term of these factors is real, and by making \[ \pm a = p \pm \sqrt{(p^2 - q)}, \] we have the functions of the form \[ x^n = a^n \] to decompose into factors. When \( p^2 < q \), then we put \( q = a^n, q = b^n, x = by, \) and the function becomes \[ b^{2n} y^{2n} + 2a^n b^n y^n + b^n \] \[ = b^{2n} (y^n + 2a^n b^n y^n + 1); \] but the condition \( p^2 < q \), or \( a^n < b^n \), makes \( a^n < b^n, \) and \( \frac{a^n}{b^n} < 1 \), therefore \( \frac{a^n}{b^n} \) may be represented by the cosine of a given arch \( \delta \), and the proposed function will be reduced to \[ b^{2n} (y^n + 2y^n \cos \delta + 1), \] we have then only to resolve the equation \[ y^n + 2y^n \cos \delta + 1 = 0, \] and we immediately find \[ y^n = \cos \delta \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \delta; \] we now assume, as in § 121, \[ y = \cos \alpha \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \alpha; \] then we find (\$ 120), \[ y^n = \cos n \alpha \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin n \alpha, \] which expression for \( y^n \), being compared with its other value, gives \[ \cos n \alpha = \cos \delta, \sin n \alpha = \sin \delta. \] These relations will be satisfied if we suppose \( n = 2m + \delta, m \) being any whole number whatever, for \[ \cos (2m \pi + \delta) = \cos \delta, \sin (2m \pi + \delta) = \sin \delta; \] we have therefore \[ z = \frac{2m \pi + \delta}{n}, \] \[ y = \cos \frac{2m \pi + \delta}{n} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{2m \pi + \delta}{n}. \] The factors of the first degree of the function \[ y^n + 2y^n \cos \delta + 1 \] will consequently be comprehended in this formula, \[ y = \left\{ \cos \frac{2m \pi + \delta}{n} \pm \sqrt{-1} \sin \frac{2m \pi + \delta}{n} \right\}. \] If \( p \) the coefficient of the second term of the proposed function be negative, the only change necessary is to make \( p = -a^n \), and to take the arch \( \delta \) greater than a <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-QUADRANT">quadrant</a>. Of the Fluents of Irrational Functions. 125. When a fluxionary expression involves irrational functions, we must endeavour either to transform it into another that is rational, or to reduce it to a series of irrational terms of this form \( Ax^n x \), and then, in either case its fluent may be found by the rules already delivered. Let us take for example the fluxion \( \frac{(1 + \sqrt{x}) - \sqrt{x^3})x}{1 + x^3} \). It is evident that by putting \( x = x^5 \), all the extractions indicated by the radical signs may be effected, and the fluxion may be transformed to \( \frac{6x^5(1 + x^3 - x^4)x}{1 + x^3} \), which, by dividing the numerator by \( 1 + x^3 \), may be otherwise expressed thus, \[ -6(x^7 - x^5 - x^4 + x^3 - x^2 + x - \frac{x}{1 + x^3}). \] The fluent of which is \[ -6 \left\{ \frac{x^8}{8} - \frac{x^7}{7} - \frac{x^6}{6} + \frac{x^5}{5} - \frac{x^4}{4} \right\} + \text{const}. \] We shall first consider such fluxions as contain the irrational function \( \sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)} \), and which have necessarily one or other of these forms, \[ X \frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}} \right), \] \( X \) being put for any rational function of \( x \); and it may be remarked, that the latter form comprehends the former, which may be written thus: \[ X \frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}} \right) \] and here the numerator of the fluxion is a rational function of \( x \). Before we transform the expression \( \sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)} \) into another that is rational with respect to the variable quantity it contains, we shall put the quantity \( A+Bx+Cx^2 \) under this form, \[ C \left( \frac{A}{C} + \frac{B}{C} x + x^2 \right); \] and, in order to abridge, we shall put \[ C = c^2, \quad \frac{A}{C} = a, \quad \frac{B}{C} = b, \] then we have \[ \sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)} = c \sqrt{(a+bx+x^2)}. \] Let us now assume \( \sqrt{(a+bx+x^2)} = x + z \), then squaring both sides of the equation, we find \( a+bx = 2xz+z^2 \), hence we get \( z = \frac{a-x^2}{2x-b} \), and consequently \[ \sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)} = c (x+z) = c \left( \frac{a-bx+x^2}{2x-b} \right). \] By means of these values the fluxion \[ X \frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}} \right) \] is transformed into another fluxion \( Z \dot{x} \), where \( Z \) denotes a rational function of \( x \), which is real when \( C \) or \( c^2 \) is positive; but as when \( C \) is negative \( c \) becomes imaginary, the fluxion \( Z \dot{x} \) which involves \( c \) becomes also imaginary. In this case we have to consider \( \sqrt{(A+Bx-Cx^2)} \), and making \[ C = c^2, \quad \frac{A}{C} = a, \quad \frac{B}{C} = b, \] it becomes \( c \sqrt{(a+bx-x^2)} \). The quantity \( x^2-bx-a \) may always be decomposed into real factors of the first degree; let us represent these factors by \( x-\alpha \), and \( x-\beta \), then it is evident that \[ a+bx-x^2 = (x-\alpha)(x-\beta). \] Let us now assume \[ \sqrt{(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)} = (x-\alpha)x, \] then squaring both sides of the equation it becomes divisible by \( x-\alpha \), and we have \( x-\alpha = (x-\alpha)x^2 \), from which we find \[ x = \frac{\alpha x^2 + \alpha'}{x^2 + 1}, \quad (x-\alpha) = \frac{\alpha' - \alpha}{x^2 + 1}, \] values which render the proposed fluxion \[ X \frac{d}{dx} \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}} \right) \] rational. Let us now take for example the fluxion \[ \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}}; \quad \text{by applying to it the first of the preceding transformations it becomes } \frac{-2z}{c(2z-b)}, \] the fluent of which is \( -\frac{1}{c} \left( 2z-b \right) + \text{const.} \) Substituting now for \( z \) its value \( x + \sqrt{(a+bx+x^2)} \), and for \( x, b, \) and \( c, \) the quantities they severally represent, the fluent becomes \[ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{C}} \left\{ \frac{1}{\sqrt{C}} \left( \frac{-B}{\sqrt{C}} - 2x\sqrt{C} \right) \right\} + \text{const.} \] a result to which we may also give this form, \[ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{C}} \left\{ \frac{-B}{2\sqrt{C}} - x\sqrt{C} + \sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)} \right\} + \text{const.} \] By uniting the constant quantities into one, and observing that the radical quantity \( \sqrt{C} \) may have the sign prefixed to it, we have at last \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)}} \text{ equal to } \frac{1}{\sqrt{C}} \left\{ \frac{B}{2\sqrt{C}} + x\sqrt{C} + \sqrt{(A+Bx+Cx^2)} \right\} + \text{const.} \] Let us take for the second example \[ \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(A+Bx-Cx^2)}}. \quad \text{By employing the latter transformation of § 126, we have } \frac{-2z}{c(z^2+1)}, \] of which the fluent is \[ -\frac{2}{c} \text{ arc } (\tan^{-1} x) + \text{const.} \] Substituting now instead of \( z \) its value \[ \frac{\sqrt{(x-\alpha)}}{\sqrt{(x-\beta)}} \text{ deduced from the equation } x-\alpha = (x-\alpha)x^2, \] Inverse Method. and putting \( \sqrt{C} \) for \( c \), we get \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(A+Bx-Cx^2)}} \] equal to \[ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{C}} \arctan \left( \frac{\sqrt{a-x}}{\sqrt{a+x}} \right) + \text{const.} \] \( a \) and \( a' \) being the roots of the equation \[ x^2 - \frac{B}{C} x - \frac{A}{C} = 0. \] Let us suppose that \( A = C = 1 \) and \( B = 0 \), then the proposed fluxion becomes in this particular case \[ \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(1-x^2)}}, \] and the preceding formula gives for its fluent \( -2 \arctan \) \[ \left( \tan^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{1-x}}{\sqrt{1+x}} \right) + \text{const.} \] for \( a \) and \( a' \) being the roots of the equation \( x^2 - 1 = 0 \), we must take \( a = -1 \), and \( a' = 1 \). We may, however, give this fluent another form by proceeding thus: Let \( v \) be the arch whose tan. \[ = \frac{\sqrt{1-x}}{\sqrt{1+x}}, \] then \( \tan^2 v = \frac{1-x}{1+x} \), and \( x = \frac{1-\tan^2 v}{1+\tan^2 v} \) \[ = \frac{2}{1+\tan^2 v} - 1 = 2 \cos^2 v - 1, \] but \[ 2 \cos^2 v - 1 = \cos 2v (\text{ALGEBRA}, § 358), \] therefore, \( x = \cos 2v \). Put \( s \) for the arch whose sine is \( x \), and \( \pi \) for half the circumference, then \( x = \cos \left( \frac{1}{2} \pi - s \right) \), therefore \( 2v = \frac{1}{2} \pi - s \), and since it has been shown that \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(1-x^2)}} = -2v + \text{const.} \] therefore \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(1-x^2)}} = s - \frac{1}{2} \pi + \text{const.} \] or, by including the arch \( \frac{1}{2} \pi \) in the constant quantity, \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(1-x^2)}} = s + \text{const.} \] This conclusion agrees with what has been shown in § 59. Instead of finding the fluent of \[ \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(A+Bx-Cx^2)}} = \frac{\dot{x}}{c\sqrt{(a+bx-x^2)}} \] by first transforming it to a rational expression, we may reduce it directly to an arch of a circle by proceeding as follows. Put \( x = \frac{b}{2} \), then \( \dot{x} = \dot{z} \), and the fluxion \[ \frac{\dot{z}}{\sqrt{(a+bx-x^2)}}; \] again, put \( a + bx = g^2 \), and \( z = g u \), then \( \dot{z} = g \dot{u} \), and this last fluxion is transformed to \[ \frac{\dot{u}}{c\sqrt{(1-u^2)}}, \] the fluent of which is \( \frac{1}{c} \) \[ \text{arc} (\sin = u) + \text{const.} \] Of the Fluents of Binomial Fluxions. 129. Let us now consider such fluxions as have this form, \[ x^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^n}}, \] and which are sometimes called binomial fluxions. We may here suppose \( m \) and \( n \) to be whole numbers, without affecting the generality of the expression. For if we had \( x^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^n}} \), we may assume \( x = z^p \), then \( \dot{x} = pz^{p-1} \), and the fluxion becomes \( 6z^{p-1} \) \[ (a+bx)^n. \] We may also suppose \( n \) to be positive, for if it were negative, so that the fluxion were \( x^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^{-n}}} \), we have only to assume \( x = \frac{1}{z} \), and the fluxion is transformed to \( -z^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+zx)^n}} \). Let us inquire in what case the fluxion \( x^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^n}} \) may become rational. Assume \( a + bx = z^q \), then \( (a+bx)^n = z^{qn} \), \( x = \frac{z^q-a}{b} \), \( x^n = \left( \frac{z^q-a}{b} \right)^n \), and \( x^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^n}} = \frac{q}{nb} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(z^q-a)^n}} \); hence the proposed fluxion is transformed to \[ \frac{q}{nb} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(z^q-a)^n}}; \] this expression is evidently rational as often as \( \frac{m}{n} \) is a whole number. There are yet other cases in which the fluxion may become rational, and which may be determined by assuming \( a + bx = z^m \), thus we have \[ x = \frac{a}{u-b}, \quad x^n = \frac{a^n}{(u-b)^n}, \] and because that \( (a-bx)^n \) \[ = \frac{a^n}{(u-b)^n} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(u-b)^n}}, \] the fluxion \( x^{m-1} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^n}} \) is transformed to \[ \frac{qa^n}{nb} \cdot \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(u-b)^n}}, \] an expression which is rational if \( \frac{m}{n} + \frac{p}{q} \) is a whole number. 130. As it is not possible, in every case, to express in finite terms the formula \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(a+bx)^n}} \), we may try to reduce it to its most simple case, as we have done. have succeeded in reducing to \( \int \frac{z}{x^2 + \beta^2} \). To effect this reduction, we remark, that, since when \( u \) and \( v \) denote any functions of a variable quantity, the fluxion of \( uv \) is \( uv + vu \), (\$37.) therefore \( \int u = u - \int vu \). Now if we can decompose the expression \( x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) into two factors, such that we can find the fluent of one of them, then denoting that factor by \( v \), and the other by \( u \), the fluent of the proposed fluxion will be made to depend on that of \( v \), which in some cases will be more simple than the proposed fluxion. That we may abridge a little the results, we shall write \( p \) instead of \( \frac{p}{q} \), so that \( p \) will represent any fraction; the proposed fluxion thus simplified in its form is \[ x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p. \] Among the different ways of resolving this fluxion into two factors, we shall choose that which diminishes the exponent of \( x \) without the parentheses, we therefore write the fluxion thus \[ x^{m-n} \cdot x^{n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p, \] now the fluent of the factor \( x^{m-n} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) may always be determined, whatever be the value of \( p \), by § 108; let us denote this factor by \( v \), then \[ v = \frac{(a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{(p+1)nb}, \quad \text{and} \quad u = x^{m-n}, \] thus the formula \( \int u = u - \int vu \) give us \( \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) equal to \[ \frac{x^{m-n} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{(p+1)nb}. \] But \( \int x^{m-n} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p+1} = \) \[ \int x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \cdot (a + bx^n) = \] \[ a \int x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p + \] \[ b \int x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p. \] Substituting now this last value in the preceding equation, and collecting into one the terms involving the fluent \( \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \), we find \[ \left(1 + \frac{m-n}{(p+1)n}\right) \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p = \] \[ \frac{1}{(p+1)nb} \left\{ x^{m-n} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p+1} - \] \[ a(m-n) \int x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \right\} \] hence at last we get (A) \[ \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p = \] \[ \frac{1}{b(pn+m)} \left\{ x^{m-n} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p+1} - \] \[ a(m-n) \int x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \right\} \] It is easy to see that, as we have, by this formula, reduced the determination of the fluent of \( x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) to that of \( x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \), we may reduce this last to that of \( x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) by writing \( m-n \) in place of \( m \) in equation (A), then by changing \( m \) into \( m-2 \) we may reduce the fluent of \( x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) to that of \( x^{m-n-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \), and so on. In general, if \( r \) denote the number of reductions, we shall at last come to \[ \int x^{m-r-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p, \quad \text{and the last formula will be} \] \[ \frac{x^{m-r} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{b(pn+m-(r-1)n)} \] \[ - \frac{a(m-rn) \int x^{m-r-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p}{b(pn+m-(r-1)n)}. \] It appears by the last formula, that if \( m \) is a multiple of \( n \), then \( \int x^{m-r} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) will be an algebraic quantity, for in that case the coefficient \( m-rn \) will be \( = 0 \), and therefore the term containing \( \int x^{m-r-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) will vanish. This result coincides with what we have already found, § 129. 131. We may also obtain a reduction, by which the exponent \( p \) will be diminished by unity. For this purpose it is sufficient to observe that \( \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^p \) is equal to \[ \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p-1} \cdot (a + bx^n) = \] \[ a \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p-1} + \] \[ b \int x^{m-1} \cdot (a + bx^n)^{p-1}, \] and that the formula (A) by changing \( m \) into \( m+n \), and \( p \) into \( p-1 \) gives Substitute now this value in the preceding equation, we have (B) \[ \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p = \frac{x^m (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{pa} + \frac{(m+n)p}{pa} \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p \] By means of this general formula we may take away successively from \( p \) as many units as it contains, and by the application of this formula, and formula (A), we may cause the fluent \( \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p \) to depend on \[ \int x^{m-r} (a + bx^n)^{p-r}, \quad r \text{ being the greatest multiple of } r \text{ contained in } m-1, \text{ and } s \text{ the greatest whole number contained in } p. \] The fluent \( \int x^2 (a + bx^3)^{\frac{3}{2}} \), for example, may, by the application of formula (A), be reduced successively to \[ \int x^2 (a + bx^3)^{\frac{3}{2}}, \quad \text{and} \quad \int x^2 (a + bx^3)^{\frac{3}{2}}. \] and by formula (B) \( \int x^2 (a + bx^3)^{\frac{3}{2}} \) is reduced successively to \[ \int x^2 (a + bx^3)^{\frac{3}{2}}, \quad \text{and} \quad \int x^2 (a + bx^3)^{\frac{3}{2}}. \] 132. It is evident, that if \( m \) and \( n \) were negative, the formulas (A) and (B) would not answer the purpose for which they have been investigated, because, in that case, they would increase the exponents instead of diminishing them. If, however, we reverse them, we shall find that they then apply to the case under consideration. From formula (A) we get \[ \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p = \frac{x^m (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{a(m-n)} - \frac{b(m+n)p}{a(m-n)} \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p; \] Substitute now \( m+n \) in place of \( m \), and it becomes (C) \[ \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p = \frac{x^m (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{am} - \frac{b(m+n)p}{am} \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p; \] This formula diminishes the exponents without the parentheses, because \( m+n-1 \) becomes \( -m+n-1 \), when \( -m \) is substituted instead of \( m \). To reverse formula (B) we first take \[ \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p = \frac{x^m (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{pa} + \frac{(m+n)p}{pa} \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p; \] Then, writing \( p+1 \) instead of \( p \), we find (D) \[ \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p = \frac{x^m (a + bx^n)^{p+1}}{(p+1)na} + \frac{(m+n)p}{(p+1)na} \int x^{m-1} (a + bx^n)^p; \] This formula answers the purpose we have in view, because \( p+1 \) becomes \( -p+1 \) when \( p \) is negative. These formulas (A), (B), (C), (D), are inapplicable when their denominators vanish. This is the case with formula (A); for example, when \( m=-np \); but, in every such case, the proposed fluxion may have its fluent determined either algebraically or by logarithms. 133. Let the fluent be \( \int \frac{x^{m-1}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}, \quad m \text{ being a whole positive number. Formula (A) immediately applies to this case, so that by putting } a=1, b=-1, n=2, p=\frac{m}{2}, \text{ we have} \] \[ \int \frac{x^{m-1}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \begin{cases} \frac{x^m \sqrt{1-x^2}}{m-1} \\ + \frac{m-2}{m-1} \int \frac{x^{m-2}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{cases} \] or, substituting \( m \) in place of \( m-1 \), \[ \int \frac{x^m}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \begin{cases} \frac{x^m \sqrt{1-x^2}}{m} \\ + \frac{m-1}{m} \int \frac{x^{m-1}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{cases} \] Let us suppose, for example, that \( m = 1 \), then \[ \int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = -\sqrt{1-x^2} + \text{const.} \] Let us now suppose that \( m = 3 \), then \[ \int \frac{x^3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \left\{ \begin{<a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-ARRAY">array</a>}{l} -\frac{1}{2}x^2\sqrt{1-x^2} \\ +\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{array} \right. \] or, substituting for \( \int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \) its value, \[ \int \frac{x^3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = -\left( \frac{1}{2}x^2 + \frac{2}{3} \right)\sqrt{1-x^2} + \text{const.} \] If we suppose \( m = 2 \), then \[ \int \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -\frac{1}{2}x\sqrt{1-x^2} \\ +\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{array} \right. \] But we have already found, § 128, that \[ \int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \text{arc}(\sin^{-1} x), \] therefore, putting \( A \) for \( \text{arc}(\sin^{-1} x) \), \[ \int \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = -\frac{1}{2}x\sqrt{1-x^2} + \frac{1}{2}A + \text{const.} \] In the very same way we find that \[ \int \frac{x^4}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \text{ is equal to } \] \[ -\left( \frac{1}{4}x^4 + \frac{3}{8}x^2 \right)\sqrt{1-x^2} + \frac{3}{8}A + \text{const.} \] 134. In the case of \( m \), a negative number, we must have recourse to formula (C), from which we find \[ \int \frac{x^{m-1}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -\frac{x^m}{m}\sqrt{1-x^2} \\ +\frac{m-1}{m}\int \frac{x^{m-1}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{array} \right. \] which formula, by writing \( -m \) instead of \( -m-1 \), becomes \[ \int \frac{x^m}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -\frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{(m-1)x^{m-1}} \\ +\frac{m-2}{m-1}\int \frac{x^{m-2}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{array} \right. \] We cannot here suppose \( m = 1 \), for that value would render the denominator \( = 0 \); therefore, before we can apply this formula, it is necessary to investigate the fluent of \( \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \). We may easily find it from § 126, or otherwise thus, put \( 1-x^2 = z^2 \), then \[ x = \sqrt{1-z^2}, \quad \dot{x} = \frac{-z\dot{z}}{\sqrt{1-z^2}}. \] Therefore \[ \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \frac{-z\dot{z}}{1-z^2} = \frac{-z\dot{z}}{1+2} = \frac{-z\dot{z}}{1-\infty}. \] The fluent of the right <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-HAND">hand</a> side of this equation is evidently (\$ 103.) \[ -\frac{1}{2}l.(1+z)+\frac{1}{2}l.(1-z) = -\frac{1}{2}l.\left( \frac{1+z}{1-z} \right); \] or, since \( \frac{1+z}{1-z} = \frac{(1+z)^2}{1-z^2} \), the same fluent may be expressed thus, \[ -\frac{1}{2}l.\frac{(1+z)^2}{1-z^2} = l.\frac{1+z}{\sqrt{1-z^2}}; \] therefore, by substituting \( \sqrt{1-x^2} \) for \( z \), and \( x \) for \( \sqrt{1-x^2} \), we have \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = -l.\left( \frac{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x} \right) + \text{const.} \] If we suppose \( m = 2 \), the formula becomes \[ \int \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x} + \text{const.} \] If we suppose \( m = 3 \), then \[ \int \frac{x^3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -\frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2x^2} \\ +\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \end{array} \right. \] which expression, by substituting for \[ \int \frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \text{ its value, becomes } \] \[ \int \frac{x^3}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} = \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -\frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2x^2} \\ +\frac{1}{2}\left( \frac{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x} \right) \end{array} \right. \] + const. Of Finding Fluents by Series. 135. We can always easily find an expression for the fluent \( \int X \dot{x} \), where \( X \) denotes any function of \( x \); when that function is expanded into a series, each term of which is some power of \( x \) multiplied by a constant quantity; thus suppose \[ X = Ax^n + Bx^{n+a} + Cx^{n+a} + \text{&c.} \] then \( X \dot{x} \) is equal to \[ Ax^n \dot{x} + Bx^{n+a} \dot{x} + Cx^{n+a} \dot{x} + \text{&c.} \] and taking the fluent of each term by § 101, \[ \int x^n = \frac{A}{m+1} x^{n+1} + \frac{B}{m+n+1} x^{n+2} + \cdots + \text{const}. \] If in the development of \( x \) there be any term of this form \( \frac{A}{x} \), the fluent corresponding to that term will be \[ A \cdot x (\text{§ 103}). \] 136. The most simple function of \( x \) that can be expanded into a series is \( \frac{1}{a+x} \), which becomes \[ \frac{1}{a} - \frac{x}{a^2} + \frac{x^2}{a^3} - \frac{x^3}{a^4} + \cdots. \] Hence we find \[ \frac{\dot{x}}{a+x} = \frac{\dot{x}}{a} - \frac{\dot{x}^2}{a^2} + \frac{\dot{x}^3}{a^3} - \frac{\dot{x}^4}{a^4} + \cdots. \] and taking the fluents \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{a+x} = \frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^2}{2a^2} + \frac{x^3}{3a^3} - \frac{x^4}{4a^4} + \cdots + \text{const}. \] Now we know that \( \int \frac{\dot{x}}{a+x} = l.(a+x) (\text{§ 57}) \) therefore \[ l.(a+x) = \frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^2}{2a^2} + \frac{x^3}{3a^3} - \frac{x^4}{4a^4} + \cdots + \text{const}. \] To find the value of the constant quantity we have only to make \( x=0 \), for then the equation becomes \( l.a = \text{const.} \) therefore \[ l.(a+x) = l.a + \frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^2}{2a^2} + \frac{x^3}{3a^3} - \cdots. \] hence, if we subtract \( l.a \) from each side, and observe that \( l.(x+a)-l.a=l.\left(\frac{x+a}{a}\right)=l.\left(1+\frac{x}{a}\right) \) we get \[ l.\left(1+\frac{x}{a}\right) = \frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^2}{2a^2} + \frac{x^3}{3a^3} - \frac{x^4}{4a^4} + \cdots. \] From this conclusion we may deduce rules for computing the logarithms of numbers. 137. Let the fluxion be \( \frac{a\dot{x}}{a^2+x^2} \), which may be put under this form \( \frac{\dot{x}}{1+x^2/a^2} \), and which consequently belongs to the arch of which the tangent \( = \frac{x}{a} (\text{§ 60}) \). By reducing \( \frac{a}{a^2+x^2} \) into a series, we find \[ \frac{a}{a^2+x^2} = \frac{1}{a} - \frac{x^2}{a^3} + \frac{x^4}{a^5} - \frac{x^6}{a^7} + \cdots. \] Hence, multiply both sides by \( \dot{x} \), and taking the fluent of each term, we get \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{a^2+x^2} = \text{arc (tan. } = \frac{x}{a}) + \text{const.} = \frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^3}{3a^3} + \frac{x^5}{5a^5} - \frac{x^7}{7a^7} + \cdots + \text{const.} \] If we wish to deduce from this equation, the value of the least arch whose tangent is \( \frac{x}{a} \), it is necessary to suppress the arbitrary constant quantity, for when that arch \( = 0 \), then \( x=0 \); thus we have the arch whose tangent is \( \frac{x}{a} \) expressed by the infinite series \[ \frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^3}{3a^3} + \frac{x^5}{5a^5} - \frac{x^7}{7a^7} + \cdots. \] Let \( \pi \) denote the circumference of a circle whose diameter is unity, or half the circumference of a circle whose radius is unity, then, as the sine of 30 degrees, or \( \frac{\pi}{6} \), is \( \frac{1}{2} \), and its cosine \( \sqrt{1-\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \), we have \[ \tan \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sin \frac{\pi}{6}}{\cos \frac{\pi}{6}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}. \] Let \( \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} \) be substituted instead of \( x \) in the above series, and \( a \) be supposed \( = 1 \), thus we get \[ \frac{\pi}{6} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}} \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{3^3} + \frac{1}{5^3} - \frac{1}{7^3} + \cdots\right) \] and therefore \[ \pi = \sqrt{\frac{1}{12}} \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{3^3} + \frac{1}{5^3} - \frac{1}{7^3} + \cdots\right); \] by taking the sum of about fifteen terms of this series, we shall find \( \pi = 3.1415927 \). The determination of this number is of <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-GREAT">great</a> importance in every branch of <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol1.html#article-MATHEMATICS">mathematics</a>. 138. By proceeding with the fluxion \( \frac{x^n \dot{x}}{a^2+x^2} \), in the same manner as we have done with \( \frac{a\dot{x}}{a^2+x^2} \), we get \[ \int \frac{x^n \dot{x}}{a^2+x^2} = \frac{x^{n+1}}{(m+1)a^n} - \frac{x^{n+1}}{(m+n+1)a^n} + \frac{x^{n+1}}{(m+2n+1)a^n} + \cdots. \] This series proceeds by the positive powers of \( x \), or is an ascending series, but we may also expand \( \frac{1}{a^2+x^2} \) into a series proceeding by the negative powers of \( x \), and which will therefore be called a descending series. Thus because \[ \frac{1}{x^2+a^2} \] we have, after multiplying both sides by \( x^n \dot{x} \), and taking the fluents \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{x^n + a^n} = \frac{1}{(n-m-1)x^{n-m-2}} + \frac{a^n}{(2n-m-1)x^{n-m-1}} + \frac{a^{2n}}{(3n-m-1)x^{n-m-2}} + \text{etc.} + \text{const.} \] This last series will be convergent when \( x \) is greater than \( a \), and at the same time \( m < n \), and \( n > 1 \). But besides, that it may contain algebraic terms only, it is necessary that none of the divisors \( n-m-1, 2n-m-1, 3n-m-1, \ldots \) become zero; this circumstance will take place as often as \( m+1 \) is a multiple of \( n \), and in which case the series \( \frac{\dot{x}}{x^n - a^n} - \frac{a^n \dot{x}}{x^{n+1}} + \text{etc.} \), which is the development of the fluxion, will contain a term of this form, \[ \frac{a^n \dot{x}}{x^n}, \quad \text{the fluent of which is } a^n \ln x. \] If in this result we put \( m = 2, n = 0, \) and \( a = 1 \), we get \[ \int \frac{\dot{x}}{1 + x^2} = \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{3x^3} - \frac{1}{5x^5} + \text{etc.} + \text{const.} \] But although the expression \( \frac{\dot{x}}{1 + x^2} \) is the fluxion of the arch having \( x \) for its tangent, we must not conclude that this series is the development of that arch, for \( x \) being supposed \( = 0 \), each of the terms of the series becomes infinite. The consideration of the constant quantity added to the fluent will remove this apparent difficulty, if we remark, that to know the true value of a series, it is always necessary to begin with the case in which it is convergent. Now the series \[ -\frac{1}{n} + \frac{1}{3n} - \frac{1}{5n} + \text{etc.} \] converges so much the faster as \( x \) is greater, and it vanishes when \( x \) is infinite; but in this <a class="xref" href="vol8.html#article-EXTREME">extreme</a> case the equation \[ \arctan(x) = -\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{3x^3} - \frac{1}{5x^5} + \text{etc.} + \text{const.} \] becomes simply \( \arctan(x) = \frac{\pi}{2} = \text{const.} \), where \( \pi \) denotes half the circumference of the circle; therefore, substituting this value of the constant quantity, we have \[ \arctan(x) = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{3x^3} - \frac{1}{5x^5} + \text{etc.} \] We may easily find an expression for the fluent of the rational fraction \( \frac{U}{V} \) (\$ III.) by expanding the quantity \( \frac{U}{V} \) into a series, but the result thus obtained is in general very complicated, and seldom convergent; besides, this manner of finding the fluent is hardly of any <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-USE">use</a>, since it may be expressed by means of arches of a circle and logarithms, both of which are readily obtained from the common trigonometrical tables. 139. The fluent of \( x^{n-1} \dot{x} (a + bx^n)^p \) is easily obtained by first expanding the quantity \( (a + bx^n)^p \) into a series by the binomial theorem, then multiplying each term of that series by \( x^{n-1} \dot{x} \), and taking the fluents of the results by \$ 101. Thus we have \[ (a + bx^n)^p = \left\{ \begin{array}{c} \frac{p}{m} \frac{pb}{q} \frac{x^{m+n}}{m+n} + \frac{p(p-q)}{1.2q^2} \frac{b^2}{m+2n} \frac{x^{m+2n}}{m+2n} \\ + \frac{p(p-q)(p-2q)}{1.2.3q^3} \frac{b^3}{m+3n} \frac{x^{m+3n}}{m+3n} + \text{etc.} \end{array} \right\} + \text{const.} \] This is an ascending series, but to get a descending series we must divide \( (a + bx^n)^p \) by \( x^p \) and multiply \( x^{n-p} \dot{x} \), the remaining part of the fluxional expression, by the same quantity, thus the fluxion is transformed to \[ x^{n-p} \dot{x} (b + ax^n)^p \] the fluent of which, by proceeding as in the former case, is \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{c} \frac{p}{m} \frac{qa}{qb} \frac{x^{m+n}}{m+n} + \frac{p(p-q)}{1.2q^2} \frac{a^2}{m+2n} \frac{x^{m+2n}}{m+2n} \\ + \frac{p(p-q)(p-2q)}{1.2.3q^3} \frac{a^3}{m+3n} \frac{x^{m+3n}}{m+3n} + \text{etc.} \end{array} \right\} + \text{const.} \] either of these series may be employed if \( a \) and \( b \) are both positive, or \( q \) an odd number, but if \( q \) be an even number, the first formula becomes imaginary on account of the factor \( a^q \) if \( a^q \) be negative, and the same thing happens to the second formula if \( a^q \) be negative. 140. Let it be required to express by a series the fluent of \( \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(x-x^2)}} \). That we may develope the radical quantity \( \frac{\dot{x}}{\sqrt{(x-x^2)}} \) we put it under this form,

ESARHADDON

Pages 358-358

the son of Sennacherib, and his successor in the <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-KINGDOM">kingdom</a> of <a class="xref" href="vol3.html#article-ASSYRIA">Assyria</a>. He is said to have reigned 29 years at <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-NINEVEH">Nineveh</a>, from the year 3294 to 3322; besides which he reigned 13 years at <a class="xref" href="vol3.html#article-BABYLON">Babylon</a>, in all 42 years. He died in the year of the world 3336, and was succeeded by Saosduchinos. Esarhaddon, in the <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol3.html#article-OPINION">opinion</a> of Sir <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-ISAAC">Isaac</a> Newton, seems to be the <a class="xref" href="vol18.html#article-SARDANAPALUS">Sardanapalus</a> who died, as Cæterarchus says, of old <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol2.html#article-AGE">age</a>, after the revolt of <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SYRIA">Syria</a>; the name Sardanapalus being derived from Asserhadon Pal.

ESCALADE

Pages 358-359
or SCALADE, a furious attack of a wall or a rampart, carried on with ladders, to pass the ditch, or mount the rampart; without proceeding in form, breaking ground, or carrying on regular works to secure the men. When the troops are prepared to pass the ditch, either with the assistance of boards, hurdles, and fascines, when it is muddy, or with small boats of tin, or baskets covered with skins or oil cloth, when it is deep and filled with water, a party must be placed on the counterscarp, opposite to the landing-place, ready to fire at the garrison if they are alarmed, and oppose the mounting on the rampart. If the ditch is dry, the ladders are fixed in some place farthest distant from the enemy; and as soon as they get upon the rampart, they put themselves in order to receive the enemy; if the enemy should be surprised and silently overcome, the detachment hastens to break open the gate, and to let in the rest of the party. If the ditch is wet, the rampart high, and provided with a revetement, it will be difficult to surprise the town in this way; but if there is no revetment, the troops may hide themselves along the outside of the rampart till all are over. Since the invention and use of gunpowder, and the walls of cities have been flanked, they are seldom taken by escalade.

ESCALLONIA

Pages 359-359

a genus of <a class="xref" href="vol16.html#article-PLANTS">plants</a> belonging to the pentandra class. See **<a class="xref" href="vol4.html#article-BOTANY">Botany</a> <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol0.html#article-INDEX">Index</a>**.

ESCAPE

Pages 359-359

in <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-LAW">Law</a>; a violent <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-OR">or</a> privy evasion out of some lawful restraint, without being delivered by due course of law. There are two sorts of escapes, voluntary and negligent. Voluntary, when a <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-MAN">man</a> arrests another for felony or other crime, and afterwards lets him go freely by consent; in which <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-CASE">case</a>, the party that permits such escape is held guilty, committed, and must answer for it. Negligent escape, on the contrary, is where one is arrested, and afterwards escapes against the <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-WILL">will</a> of the person that arrested him, and is not pursued with fresh <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SUIT">suit</a>, and retaken before the person pursuing hath lost sight in him. By stat. 8 and 9 Will. III. c. 26, the keepers of <a class="xref" href="vol6.html#article-PRISONS">prisons</a> conniving at escapes shall forfeit 500l.; and in civil <a class="xref" href="../1778/vol3.html#article-CASES">cases</a> the <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol3.html#article-SHERIFF">sheriff</a> is answerable for the debt.

ESCHAR

Pages 359-359

in <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-SURGERY">Surgery</a>, the crust <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-OR">or</a> scab occasioned by burns or caustic medicines.

ESCHARA

Pages 359-359

in <a class="xref" href="vol14.html#article-NATURAL_HISTORY"><a class="xref"</a> href="vol14.html#article-NATURAL">Natural</a> <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol6.html#article-HISTORY">History</a>, the name of a <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-SPECIES">species</a> of coralline, &c. The <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-CHARACTERS">characters</a> of which are these: they are of a stony <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-OR">or</a> coral-like <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-HARDNESS">hardness</a>, and resemble a woven cloth in their texture; and the <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol15.html#article-MICROSCOPE">microscope</a> informs us, that they consist of arrangements of very small cells, whose surfaces appear much in that form. Linnæus makes it a species of millepora, in the class of lithophytes.

ESCHEAT

Pages 359-359

in Scots <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-LAW">Law</a>, is that forfeiture which is incurred upon a person's being denounced a rebel. See Law, <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-PART">Part</a> III. No clxvi. 12.

ESCHEVIN

Pages 359-359
or **Echevin** (Scabinus), in the French and Dutch polity, a magistrate elected by the inhabitants of a city, to take care of their common concerns, the good order, conveniency, and decoration of the city, &c. At Paris there were formerly a prevôt and four eschevins; in most other cities a mayor and eschevins. In Languedoc, Provence, and Dauphiné, they were called consuls at Toulouse, capitouls; and jurats at Bordeaux. Anciently the eschevins were the assessors and counsellors of the comites or judges of cities; on which account they were called in some places pairs, pares; they even took cognizance of petty causes themselves. Du Cange observes, that the judges and their assessors, who were chosen by the inhabitants, were called scabini, "eschevins," and their college scabinagium or "eschevinage." "In Holland, the scabini or eschevins judge of all civil affairs at first hand. They also take cognizance of criminal matters: and if the criminal confess himself guilty, they can see their sentence executed without appeal. They can even give torture. The number is not the same in all cities; at Amsterdam there are nine, at Rotterdam seven, &c.

ESCHRAKITES

Pages 359-359
or **Esrakites**, a sect of philosophers, among the Mahometans, who adhere to the doctrines and opinions of Plato. The word is derived from the Arabic prw schraca, which in the fourth conjugation prw schraca, signifies "to shine, glitter like the sun," so that Eschrakite seems to import "illumined." The Eschrakites, or Mahometan Platonists, place their highest good and happiness in the contemplation of the Divine Majesty; despising the gross imaginations of the Alcoran touching paradise. They are very careful in avoiding all vice; they preserve an equal and easy temper, love music, and divert themselves with composing little poems or spiritual songs. The sheickis or priests, and the chief among the preachers of the imperial mosques, are Eschrakites.

ESCLAIRCISSEMENT

Pages 359-359

a French <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-TERM">term</a> adopted into our <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-LANGUAGE">language</a>, signifying the explaining <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-OR">or</a> clearing up of some difficulty or obscurity.

ESCORT

Pages 359-359

a French <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-TERM">term</a>, sometimes used in English authors to denote a convoy <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-OR">or</a> <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol7.html#article-COMPANY">company</a> of armed men, attending some person or thing, in a journey or voyage, to defend or secure it from insults. Some derive the word from the Latin cohors.

ESCOUADE

Pages 359-359
or **Squad**, is usually the third or fourth part of a company of foot; so divided for mounting guards, and for the more convenient relieving of one another. It is equivalent to brigade of a troop of horse. See BRIGADE.

ESCUAGE

Pages 359-359

in our old customs, a kind of <a class="xref" href="../1778/vol0.html#article-KNIGHTHOOD">knighthood</a>, called <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-SERVICE">service</a> of the shield, by which the tenant was bound to follow his <a class="xref" href="vol12.html#article-LORD">lord</a> to the wars on his own <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol6.html#article-CHARGE">charge</a>. See the <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-ARTICLES">articles</a> CHIVALRY, Feudal System, and <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-KNIGHT">Knight</a>-Service. **ESCOLAPIUS**. See Esculapius.

ESCULENT

Pages 359-359

an appellation given to such <a class="xref" href="vol16.html#article-PLANTS">plants</a>, <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-OR">or</a> the roots of them, as may be eaten: such are beets, <a class="xref" href="../1771/vol0.html#article-CARROTS">carrots</a>, artichokes, leeks, onions, parsnips, potatoes, radishes, scorzonera, &c.

ESCURIAL

Pages 359-360

a <a class="xref" href="vol18.html#article-ROYAL">royal</a> residence of <a class="xref" href="vol6.html#article-SPAIN">Spain</a>, situated about 15 miles <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-NORTH">north</a>-west of <a class="xref" href="vol12.html#article-MADRID">Madrid</a>. It is the largest and most superb structure in the whole <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-KINGDOM">kingdom</a>, and perhaps one of the finest in <a class="xref" href="vol8.html#article-EUROPE">Europe</a>. The word is Arabic, meaning "a <a class="xref" href="vol16.html#article-PLACE">place</a> full of rocks." It is built in a dry barren spot, surrounded with rugged <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-MOUNTAINS">mountains</a>, insomuch that every thing which grows there is owing to art. This place was chosen, it is said, for the sake of the <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-STONE">stone</a> wherewith the fabric was built, which is got from a mountain <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-JUST">just</a> by, and is very durable; and the <a class="xref" href="vol7.html#article-DESIGN">design</a> of erecting it was to commemorate a victory which <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-PHILIP">Philip</a> II. obtained over the French (but by the assistance of the English forces) at St Quintin, on St Laurence's <a class="xref" href="vol7.html#article-DAY">day</a>, in the year 1557. The Spanish <a class="xref" href="vol7.html#article-DESCRIPTION">description</a> of this structure forms a sizeable quarto volume, and it is said that its founder expended upon it six millions of ducats. The apartments are decorated with an astonishing variety of paintings, <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-SCULPTURE">sculpture</a>, <a class="xref" href="vol20.html#article-TAPESTRY">tapestry</a>, ornaments of <a class="xref" href="vol9.html#article-GOLD">gold</a> and silver, marble, jasper, gems, and other curious <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-STONES">stones</a>, surpassing all imagination. This <a class="xref" href="vol4.html#article-BUILDING">building</a>, besides its <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-PALACE">palace</a>, contains a <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol6.html#article-CHURCH">church</a>, <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol13.html#article-LARGE">large</a> and richly ornamented; a <a class="xref" href="vol13.html#article-MAUSOLEUM">mausoleum</a>; cloisters; a convent; a <a class="xref" href="../1842/vol7.html#article-COLLEGE">college</a>; and a library, containing about 30,000 volumes; besides large apartments for all kinds of artists and <a class="xref" href="vol13.html#article-MECHANICS">mechanics</a>, noble walks, with extensive parks and gardens, beautified with fountains and costly ornaments. The fathers that live in the convent are 200, and they have an annual revenue of 12,000l. It was begun by Philip in 1562, five years after the <a class="xref" href="vol3.html#article-BATTLE">battle</a>; and completed in 22 years. It consists of several courts and quadrangles, which altogether are disposed in the shape of a gridiron, the <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-INSTRUMENT">instrument</a> of the martyrdom of St Laurence: the apartments where the <a class="xref" href="vol11.html#article-KING">king</a> resides form the handle. The building is a <a class="xref" href="vol12.html#article-LONG">long</a> <a class="xref" href="vol19.html#article-SQUARE">square</a> of 640 by 580, and the height up to the <a class="xref" href="vol18.html#article-ROOF">roof</a> is all round 60 feet, except on the garden side, where the ground is more taken away. At each <a class="xref" href="vol2.html#article-ANGLE">angle</a> is a square tower 200 feet <a class="xref" href="vol0.html#article-HIGH">high</a>. The <a class="xref" href="vol15.html#article-NUMBER">number</a> of windows in the west <a class="xref" href="vol9.html#article-FRONT">front</a> is 200; in the east front 366. The orders employed are Doric and Ionic. There are three doors in the <a class="xref" href="vol17.html#article-PRINCIPAL">principal</a> front. Over the <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-GRAND">grand</a> entrance are the arms of Spain, carved in stone; and a little higher in a niche, a statue of St Laurence in a deacon's <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-HABIT">habit</a>, with a gilt gridiron in his <a class="xref" href="vol18.html#article-RIGHT">right</a> <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-HAND">hand</a>, and a book in his left. Directly over the door is a <a class="xref" href="vol3.html#article-BASSO_RELIEVO">basso-relievo</a> of two enormous gridirons in stone. This vast structure, however, with its narrow high towers, small windows, and steep sloping roof, exhibits a very uncouth style of <a class="xref" href="vol2.html#article-ARCHITECTURE">architecture</a>; at the same times that the domes, and the immense <a class="xref" href="vol8.html#article-EXTENT">extent</a> of its fronts, render it a wonderfully grand object from every point of view. The church, which is in the centre of all, is large, awful, and richly but not affectedly ornamented. The cupola is bold and <a class="xref" href="vol12.html#article-LIGHT">light</a>. The high altar is composed of rich marbles, agates, and jaspers of <a class="xref" href="vol10.html#article-GREAT">great</a> rarity, the produce of this kingdom.
